title: Connectivity & Ops Responsiveness Cards — compact network-first console surface
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact, network-first 'Connectivity & Ops Responsiveness' card set for the Private/VPC Console cluster list and cluster detail pages. The goal is a dense, scannable surface that surfaces: 1) current connectivity state (OK/Degraded/Partitioned), 2) estimated remediation time and recommended action (e.g., restart node pool, reroute traffic), 3) cost impact signal (delta vs baseline), and 4) quick-operate affordances (open diagnostics, run probe, start rollback). Cards must be keyboard-accessible and support hover previews for simulated traffic traces. This ticket covers low-fidelity-to-high-fidelity prototype, accessibility review, and handoff artifacts for frontend implementation.
design_decisions: Use three-tier severity chip (green/yellow/red) plus a subtle dot for transient flapping to avoid noisy full-card color fills
Prioritize inline actions over dropdowns for the top 3 most common remediation steps to reduce clicks during incidents
Expose an affordance to 'simulate traffic' on hover that renders a lightweight trace preview; full trace links to Observability console
Show cost delta as a sparklines micro-visual beneath the title to avoid taking primary visual real estate
Compact layout must collapse to a single-line list item on narrow screens while preserving semantic order (state, name, latency, cost delta, quick actions)
acceptance_criteria: Prototype available in Figma with component variants for OK/Degraded/Partitioned/flapping states
A11y checks: color contrast passes AA; keyboard focus order documented
Handoff tokens documented: spacing, chip sizes, iconography, micro-interaction timings
Engineering acceptance: annotated spec with responsive breakpoints and interaction states
Performance: interactions must render in <100ms when list contains up to 200 cards (engineering to confirm)
